facts.fact: Africa50 and Bayobab (MTN Group) announced a partnership on 15 May 2023 to co-develop Project East2West, a roughly US$320-325 million terrestrial fibre network linking landlocked countries to east and west coast subsea cables, with Angola among the twelve countries named.

systems.system: WACS, SACS and MONET submarine cables

note: Agreement links Angola Cables to a US network; no African country named at the other end, and landlocked-country benefit is only expected.

slug: 2023-06-27 Paratus to build third Angola data center (DC3, Tier IV)

facts.fact: In November 2023 Paratus secured a US$31 million debt facility from EAIF and Ninety One financing a Luanda data centre and three terrestrial fibre routes, one of them Luanda-Lusaka-Dar es Salaam, so Angola, Zambia and Tanzania are named.

facts.fact: ITWeb Africa reports, citing Angola's telecommunications ministry (MINTTICS), that Angola and Mozambique signed a bilateral memorandum in June 2026 under which Mozambique's Tmcel and TVM would use Angola's ANGOSAT-2 satellite for telecom and broadcast signals, with a commercial agreement still to be formalised.

ITWeb Africa reports that Angola's National Space Programme Management Office signed a commercial pilot agreement with Telecom Namibia to validate satellite-driven backhaul; the article gives no signing date, so the document's published date is used.

systems.owner: Angola (National Space Programme Management Office; MINTTICS announces)
systems.tiers: Tmcel and Televisao de Mocambique (Mozambique) in proof-of-concept trials; Telecom Namibia under a pilot agreement

note: Tmcel's proof-of-concept testing (announced 2026-08-25) is a trial toward a commercial agreement; the document states no service or traffic, so no service fact.
Angola-Tanzania ICT MoU only records Tanzanian interest in ANGOSAT-2 access; no agreement naming the shared facility, no building or service.

facts.fact: Angola Telecom's executive director said Angola Telecom and Telecom Namibia signed a memorandum of understanding in Swakopmund in March 2026 for the SARSSy submarine cable, with five Angolan landing points and a link to Equiano, due in service in June 2027.

Angola Telecom's executive director said a terrestrial fibre link between Angola (Santa Clara) and Namibia (Ondjiva) already exists and the two operators already provide telecom services in both directions.

O Economico reports that Angola's telecommunications minister Mario Oliveira and Mozambique's minister Americo Muchanga signed a memorandum of understanding at the V National Communications Conference for a Nacala-Lobito submarine cable, still in the concession phase.

facts.fact: Angola's communications minister said a contract was signed this year to link Angola and Namibia through the South Atlantic Regional Submarine System (SARSSY), now at the study and preparation stage.
